title: Joining Frank Dusen's band and playing snare in brass bands
summary: Bill sits in with Dusen's band at Algiers, is taken on, and talks about snare versus bass drum with Robichaud and Happy.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: And this old, this old Nancy, Lorenzo Stahl, he was using Lorenzo Stahl on a band. I remember that good. See, now that was a, that's what all he used to use around here. People call us a Dixon Lane. That been going on. Sure. For years, that been going. We were raised like that. We just didn't use no piano.

We used a bass and a violin. You had that violin there. I don't care, that violin was a leader. He used to lead the band. So I got up, I got up and I said, Nene knew that I could play. Nene said, come on, Come on little baby. Come on little baby. Come on rest me up. Come on rest me up. We get up there and we play. I got up there and I played. Frank was living in the Algeist then. That's Frank at home too, Frank at home too. Frank was living in the Algeist then. Frank said, you look right, you learn how to play good, I'm going to take you with me. I said, okay. Mr. Deuce, okay Mr. Deuce. I said, call him Mr. Deuce. So I played good, you see. And every time a band would come over there, I'd jump in there and play. Frank had took me with him. After I got good enough he took me with him. I was playing with Morgan, Sam Morgan, all the parts. It was transformed by the parts. I was drawn to see. That's midwilder.
I was going to ask some more about those early days. Some of the, when you first played in a brass band, did you play snare drum or bass drum most of the time? Snare drum.

Snare drum. I never beat a bass drum. Never did beat the bass drum. There was one time I was playing a, I was playing a parade and one of our great bass drum players, very few people know it, there was Old Man Robichaud, a violin player? Oh yes, I heard he played. Old Man Robichaud, a wonderful bass player. Old Man Robichaud was a wonderful bass player, but strictly by music. All the fumes and everything, he used to play all of that. So he taken sick. And they had Red Happy around at that time. And he called Red Happy to play the bass drum. So Red Happy, we all was in the same class, Red Happy said, I will play the bass drum, I'll play the snare drum. So I'll give you my snare drum and I took the bass drum and played a couple of novels, I said, I don't like this, Happy. I said, come on, you can do better than I can. I said, I don't like this Red, you do better than I can. That's where Red took the snare, took the bass drum. And boy, we did a cut up. Old Man, we did salsa brass, we did a cut up. Old Man Joe Rubichaud. Joe Rubichaud. That's the first time I tried to play bass drum. I can play it, but I didn't like that one beat.
